title: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinders — Year 9

header.title: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinders
header.subtitle: Unroll the can: from net to formula

meta.lesson-focus: Apply formulas V = πr²h and SA = 2πr² + 2πrh for a cylinder; derive the curved-surface area by unrolling the cylinder into a rectangle of dimensions 2πr by h; can-cooler material problems.
meta.ac9-descriptor-text: solve problems involving the volume and surface area of right prisms and cylinders using appropriate units
meta.sa-conceptual-understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts

html.section0_intro: Last lesson you found the surface area of right prisms using nets. A cylinder is a prism-like solid with a circle as its cross-section. These three questions check the skills you need today.
html.section_warmup:
A real situation that is secretly today's measurement.

Your class is raising money by selling foam can-coolers at $4 each. Foam costs money, so every cm² wasted cuts into the profit.

A can-cooler is a foam sleeve that wraps round a can. To buy the right amount of foam you need to know how much surface the sleeve covers, and to know how much drink the can holds you need its volume.

A can is a cylinder. Peel the label off and it lies flat as a rectangle. Today you work out why the curved surface is 2πrh, and use it with the volume πr2h to cost the fundraiser.

html.worked_example:
A tin of tomatoes has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Find its volume and its total surface area, as multiples of π.

1
Name the pieces
Write down r and h (halve the diameter if you are given it).
r = 3 cm, h = 10 cm
Base area = πr2 = π × 32 = 9π cm²
2
Volume = base area × height
Same idea as a prism: the cross-section is a circle.
V = πr2h = 9π × 10 = 90π cm³
3
Surface area = two ends + curved surface
The curved surface is the rectangle 2πr by h.
Two ends: 2 × 9π = 18π
Curved: 2π × 3 × 10 = 60π
Total = 18π + 60π
Answer V = 90π cm³ ≈ 283 cm³  ·  SA = 78π cm² ≈ 245 cm²

retrieval.q: A circle has radius 5 cm. Its area is A = πr2 = ___π cm². Type the number in front of π.
retrieval.hint: Area of a circle is π × r × r, so the number in front of π is 5 × 5.

retrieval.q: A rectangular prism has a base area of 12 cm² and a height of 5 cm. What is its volume in cm³?
retrieval.hint: Volume of a prism = base area × height.

retrieval.q: What is the total surface area of a cube with side length 3 cm, in cm²?
retrieval.hint: A cube has 6 identical square faces.

weDo.q: A tin has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. Area of one circular end: ___π cm². Give your answer as a multiple of π: type just the number in front of π.
weDo.hint: Area of the circular end = πr², with r = 5.

weDo.q: Volume of the same tin: ___π cm³ (base area × height).
Total surface area of the tin (two ends and the curved surface): ___π cm².
weDo.hint: Two ends: 2 × 25π = 50π. Curved surface: 2π × 5 × 12 = 120π. Add them.

fb.14: You have not squared the radius: πr² means π × r × r.
